title: A password manager makes unique passwords practical
summary: Reusing a password can let a breach at one service put other accounts at risk. A password manager helps create and remember a different strong password for each account.
body: When a password is reused across multiple services, a breach at one service can expose other accounts that use the same sign-in. Attackers may try leaked credentials on email, shopping, social and financial services.

A reputable password manager can generate and store a unique password for each account, removing the need to remember them all. Choose a strong, unique master password and turn on multi-factor authentication for the manager when available.

Account recovery matters too. Review the manager's recovery options and keep any emergency information somewhere protected. Be careful when signing in on shared devices, and do not store a work password in a personal tool if your employer's policy says otherwise.
takeaways: Use a unique password for every important account.
Protect the password manager with a strong master password and MFA.
Plan how you will recover access to the manager.
